options.approach:
Same aiclient package, same schema, same routes and flag as opt-1 — the difference is **where the provider call happens**.

1. `backend/shared/pkg/aiclient` is built as in opt-1, but only **ms-integration** instantiates it. Its outbound client uses `netguard.AdminTarget` (ADR-15) and ms-integration's existing egress conventions (`internal/client/jira/client.go`, `internal/ssrf`).
2. ms-integration gains `AICompletionService.Complete(provider_ref, messages, params)`. It resolves the credential **itself**: either the AI key column is migrated into ms-integration's credential store (`cmd/migrate-secrets` already exists as a precedent) or SS passes an opaque `model_source_id` and ms-integration reads the sealed key through the existing credential path. No plaintext key crosses a service boundary in either variant.
3. ms-system-setting keeps ENT-17 ownership, the conversation tables, the `/ai/conversation/*` handlers, `AI_ENABLED`, the per-org quota check and the usage ledger — i.e. steps 2, 4, 5, 6 of opt-1 unchanged — and calls ms-integration instead of a provider. `ListMessages`/`AppendTurn` stay in SS; `ResolveModel` becomes internal to ms-integration.
4. Metrics and the "masked key" guarantee land in one place (ms-integration is already the sensitive component with an automated boundary test, T-JS-22), and the AI provider joins Jira/Google under the same egress audit.
5. Gateway/conformance changes are identical to opt-1. Tests: aiclient unit tests in shared; an ms-integration contract test against mock-ext `/llm/v1/chat/completions`; an SS handler test with a faked completion client; a boundary test asserting SS holds no provider URL/key in memory on the chat path.
cons: ADR-09 names Jira and Google only; stretching it to LLMs is an interpretation that the architecture owner has to confirm — and the repo's own approved solution (SOL-P3c-E §3.2) puts the call in system-setting, so this option deliberately diverges from it.
Same AC-AI-05 vs NFR-CO-02 / BRL-64 / ADR-12 conflict as opt-1 (503 vs 404 + `X-Route-Missing: 1`).
An extra hop on a 60 s call: two timeout budgets, two retry layers to reconcile, and a new failure mode (ms-integration down ⇒ AI down) for a feature that otherwise has no integration dependency.
Quota/ledger lives in SS while the call lives in ms-integration, so usage accounting is no longer transactional with the provider response.
Either a key migration out of `ai_model_source` (data movement, rollback story) or a cross-service credential read — both more work than opt-1.

ms-integration is a protected-adjacent, high-risk service; `services/infrastructure/integration-hub/` is off limits per project rules, so the boundary must be checked before touching anything under `infrastructure/`.
pros: Consistent with ADR-09: credentials and egress concentrated in one sensitive, boundary-tested service, with one place to audit AI spend and destinations.
Plaintext provider keys never travel over internal gRPC, which is the weakest point of opt-1's `ResolveModel`.
Adding Claude/Bedrock or an internal gateway later changes one service, not every AI consumer.
ms-integration already has the credential encryption, SSRF and outbound-observability plumbing, so less new infrastructure code.

Nested retry layers multiply worst-case latency well past the 90 s gateway read timeout.

1. **`backend/shared/pkg/aiclient`** — `Client{Chat,Stream}`, `Provider{Name,BaseURL,APIKey,Model,Params}`; a single OpenAI Chat Completions implementation serving `Open AI`/`DeepSeek`/`ZhiPu AI` (the only three `ui/tms/src/enums/modelEnum.ts` can create); Claude/Bedrock ⇒ `ErrProviderUnsupported` ⇒ 422 plus an `AI-PROVIDER-CLAUDE-BEDROCK` row in `tools/conformance/deferred_features.yaml`. Build the client exactly as the existing guarded clients do — `netguard.NewClientFrom(netguard.FromEnv(netguard.AdminTarget), base, 60s)` + `telemetry.WrapTransport(target, …, WithUntrustedTarget())` (`backend/services/qa-core/api-test/pkg/safehttp/safehttp.go:39`, `system-setting/pkg/smtp/smtp.go:17`) — ≤2 retries on 429/5xx/timeout honouring `Retry-After` (capped + jitter); key only in `Authorization`; blocked targets keep netguard's fixed "target not allowed" text; metrics `ai_requests_total{provider,model,status}`, `ai_latency_seconds`, `ai_tokens_total{direction}`.
2. **Data** — `migrations/V037__ss_ai_conversation_v2.sql`: `ai_conversation` + `title/scene/organization_id/model_id/update_time`; new `ai_conversation_message(id, conversation_id, role, content, create_time, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_id)`; `ai_model_source` + nullable `organization_id`, `project_id`; `ai_org_quota(organization_id, period, token_limit, cost_limit_micro)` and append-only `ai_usage_ledger`. Additive only; register tables in `tools/conformance/table_owners.yaml` and grants in `deploy/*/mysql-init/10-users.sql`.
3. **Service layer** — extend `internal/usecase/ai/ai.go` with `ResolveModel` (`status=enabled`, `secret.Open`, ownerType compared after `TrimSpace`, resolution personal → project → org → system), `ListMessages`, `AppendTurn`; publish `tms/identity/v1/ai.proto AIService` on gRPC 50057 behind `svcauth.RequireCaller("case-management","api-test")` so CR-H02/BL-H03 never hold provider keys. Existing CRUD already masks (`secret.Show/Seal/Resolve`, `audit.Track`+`Redact`) ⇒ AC-3 holds unchanged.
4. **Routes** — `internal/handler/ai/conversation.go`: `POST /ai/conversation/{add,chat,update}`, `GET /ai/conversation/{list,delete/:id,chat/list/:id}`; idempotent on the client-generated `conversationId` (the SPA fires `add` without awaiting it); `chat` returns a plain string in the envelope; `httpx` never-nil lists; other users' ids ⇒ 404.
5. **Quota** — `QuotaCheck(orgID, estimate)` runs *before* `ResolveModel`: exhausted ⇒ 429 with a plain Vietnamese message and no provider call (AC-4); after a successful turn, `AppendTurn` + ledger insert + counter update in one transaction (`shared/pkg/uow`). Period = calendar month; `organizationId` arrives on the chat request and is checked against membership.
6. **Flag & gateway** — `AI_ENABLED` (default off) gates a subtree middleware returning 503; replace `gone("UF-P1a-03", …, "/ai/conversation")` at `backend/services/gateway/internal/routing/default_table.go:161` with `sub(ss, "/ai/conversation")`, read timeout ≥90 s, and update `route_decisions.approved.yaml`, `routes_golden_test.go:146`, `tools/decom/{route_classes_dec,ui_route_decisions}.yaml`, `tests/golden/ui-neutral/route_classes.json`.
7. **Tests** — aiclient units (two `Retry-After` retries then a real error; private target blocked with `netguard.AllowLoopbackForTests`); handler tests against `tests/local-stack/mock-ext` `/llm/v1/chat/completions` and `__fail`; extend the SEC-07 secret test to the AI key.
cons: AC-5's 503 contradicts BRL-64, ADR-12 and NFR-CO-02, which require an unimplemented feature to answer 404 + `X-Route-Missing: 1` and forbid 501/fake-200 routes; the exception has to be argued as "service configured off", not "deferred feature", and the UF-P1a-03 entries retired.
FR-SYS-07 as written still mandates the honest 501 for chat/transform and ENT-17 marks conversation as deferred (`hội thoại (hoãn)`); both need a revision together with this CR.

`ResolveModel` hands the decrypted key to callers over internal gRPC — safe for AC-3's UI/API/log surfaces but it widens where plaintext travels; needs an interceptor-level redaction test (NFR-SE-04).
Quota and cost semantics (tokens vs money, period, who sets the limit, multi-org users) exist nowhere in the graph or the code and must be designed inside this CR.
Per-org/project model binding has no UI: the SPA's `ownerType` enum is only `SYSTEM `/`PERSONAL`, so the new scopes are reachable only through an admin API until a UI CR lands.
A 60 s provider call plus a ≥90 s gateway read timeout holds system-setting worker slots; a chat burst can degrade unrelated SS routes.
pros: Follows the design already written and reviewed in-repo (SOL-P3c-E §3.2), including the SPA call-order race, envelope shapes and gateway requirements — little is left to invent.

Reuses existing building blocks: `netguard` (ADR-15 AdminTarget), `secretbox`/`internal/secret`, `audit.Track/Redact`, `telemetry.WrapTransport`, `uow`, the `safehttp`/`pkg/smtp` client pattern and the live `ai_model_source` CRUD.

Quota, usage, conversation and key all sit in SVC-01's own schema (ENT-17 already names system-setting as owner), so the pre-check and the ledger are one transaction with no cross-service consistency problem.
`AIService` over gRPC gives CR-H02 and BL-H03 one AI entry point instead of each service holding provider keys (keeps NFR-SE-04's blast radius small).
`AI_ENABLED=false` is a complete, instant kill switch; migrations are additive so rollback needs no data work.

**Same egress owner, different enforcement point and consistency model.**

1. **`shared/pkg/aiclient`** — identical to opt-1 (OpenAI-compatible provider, netguard `AdminTarget`, 60 s, ≤2 retries on `Retry-After`, masked key, metrics); AC-6/AC-7 are proven by the package's own tests either way.
2. **Edge flag** — `/ai/conversation` stays one entry in `backend/services/gateway/internal/routing/default_table.go`, but as a flag-aware entry: `AI_ENABLED=true` ⇒ `sub(ss, "/ai/conversation")` with a ≥90 s read timeout; `AI_ENABLED=false` ⇒ a `Disabled` mode that answers 503 for the whole subtree without touching an upstream (AC-5 in one place, for CR-H02's AI routes too). `routes_golden_test.go` gets both tables.
3. **Edge quota** — the gateway asks SS once per (org, period) for the budget over gRPC, caches it, and keeps the consumed counters in Redis (`rediskeys` namespace, same store CT-02 already uses for revocation and rate-limit); an exhausted org is refused with 429 and a clear message before the request ever reaches SS, so no provider call happens. SS re-checks the cached budget cheaply as a second line of defence.
4. **SS stays thin** — `ai_conversation` + `ai_conversation_message` migration, `ResolveModel/ListMessages/AppendTurn`, the six handlers (idempotent `add`, string-returning `chat`), and after each turn an `ai.usage.v1` outbox event (`shared/pkg/kafkax/outbox`, the mechanism BRL-64 already names) carrying tokens and estimated cost. A consumer in SS folds events into the append-only `ai_usage_ledger` and refreshes the Redis counters; a nightly job reconciles counters against the ledger.
5. **Model config** — per-org/project binding as in opt-1 (nullable `organization_id`/`project_id` on `ai_model_source`, resolution personal → project → org → system), keys unchanged (`secret.Seal/Show/Open`), so AC-3 is untouched.
6. **Tests** — gateway table tests for the flag-off 503 and the Redis refusal; SS handler tests against mock-ext; a consumer test proving the ledger converges; a reconciliation test showing drift is corrected.
cons: Splits AI policy between two owners: CT-02 gives the gateway auth, CSRF, rate-limit, route table and MCP — a per-organisation business quota at the edge stretches that responsibility and leaves SVC-01 no longer the single owner of ENT-17's rules.

Eventual consistency: between the provider call and the ledger fold an organisation can overshoot its limit, and a Redis loss either frees or falsely blocks quota — weaker than AC-4's "system does not call the provider" read in the worst case.

The same BRL-64/ADR-12/NFR-CO-02 conflict as opt-1 (503 instead of 404 + `X-Route-Missing: 1`) plus the UF-P1a-03 decision ledger, and the gateway now answers a status code for a feature it does not own.
Quota semantics still undesigned, and the budget now has to be exposed over a new gRPC call and cached coherently — more contract surface than opt-1 for the same AC.
More moving parts to stand up in the local stack and in CI (Redis counters, Kafka consumer, reconciliation job), so AC-4 regressions are harder to pin down.
pros: One switch disables every AI route (including CR-H02/BL-H03 later) without deploying a service change, and the refusal never consumes a system-setting worker.
An exhausted organisation is refused at the edge, so a quota storm cannot fill SS's slots or its DB connections.

Reuses the gateway's existing Redis rate-limit machinery (`internal/ratelimit`, `rediskeys`) and the outbox pattern BRL-64 names as the enforcement mechanism, instead of a new synchronous ledger path.
Usage accounting is append-only and off the request path, so a slow ledger write never slows or fails a chat turn.

options.approach:
**Ship the working AI path first; keep accounting as data already written.**

1. **`shared/pkg/aiclient`** — as in opt-1 (OpenAI-compatible, `netguard.AdminTarget`, 60 s, ≤2 retries on `Retry-After`, masked key, metrics, Claude/Bedrock ⇒ `ErrProviderUnsupported` + deferred row). This is the part both ACs 6 and 7 rest on, so it is built in full.
2. **Flag and limits as settings** — add a group to `backend/shared/pkg/policy/keys.go`: `policy.ai.enabled` (env `AI_ENABLED`, default `false`), `policy.ai.monthly_token_limit`, `policy.ai.monthly_cost_limit_micro`, read through the existing `policy.Reader` (DB wins over env, cached, last-good on failure). An organisation-level override lives in one narrow table `ai_org_limit(organization_id, token_limit, cost_limit_micro)`; no ledger, no counters.
3. **Usage** — `ai_conversation_message` already stores `tokens_in/tokens_out` per turn (migration `V037`), so consumption is `SUM(tokens)` for the organisation in the current month, maintained as one `ai_org_usage(organization_id, period, tokens, cost_micro)` rollup row updated in the same transaction as the turn and rebuildable from the messages at any time. The pre-check reads the rollup before `ResolveModel`, so an exhausted organisation gets 429 and no provider call (AC-4).
4. **Model scoping** — `ai_model_scope(model_id, scope_type ENUM('SYSTEM','ORG','PROJECT','PERSONAL'), scope_id)` keeps `ai_model_source` untouched; resolution personal → project → org → system. Keys keep flowing through `secret.Seal/Show/Open` and `audit.Redact` (AC-3).
5. **Routes, service, gateway** — identical to opt-1: `internal/handler/ai/conversation.go` with the six routes (idempotent `add`, string `chat`, never-nil lists, 404 for other users), `ResolveModel/ListMessages/AppendTurn` exposed over gRPC for CR-H02, and the `default_table.go:161` flip plus the governance files.
6. **Deferred to a follow-up** — provider-billing-accurate cost, per-project limits (only per-org limits ship), a separate append-only ledger, and the settings-screen UI for the new keys.
cons: Delivers less than the CR's scope asks: cost limits are estimates from a static price table and per-project limits are deferred, so part of "giới hạn chi phí và hạn mức theo tổ chức" ships in a reduced form that the requester must accept.

`policy.Defs()` drives the settings screen, so new keys appear as new rows in the UI without a registered UI exception — a direct tension with NFR-CO-01 (UI-frozen) unless the group is hidden from that screen.
No append-only usage ledger means a weaker audit trail than BRL-64's INSERT-only logging habit, and disputes about an organisation's consumption can only be resolved by re-aggregating the messages.
Same BRL-64/ADR-12/NFR-CO-02 conflict for the 503 behaviour, and FR-SYS-07/ENT-17 still need the same revision.
Rebuilding the rollup gets expensive once conversations grow, so a rollup/retention job becomes necessary sooner than in opt-1.
pros: Smallest new schema: one rollup row and one scope table instead of a ledger plus counters, and the usage figure is always rebuildable from the stored messages — nothing can silently drift.

Limits and the kill switch become admin-editable at runtime through the mechanism the platform already has (`system_parameter` + `shared/pkg/policy`), with environment defaults for a fresh install, instead of a redeploy per change.
Fastest path to a demonstrable AC-1/AC-3/AC-5/AC-6/AC-7 with mock-ext, which is what the local stack can actually verify today.
Leaves per-project limits and money-accurate cost to a follow-up once real provider billing is available, instead of guessing both now.

recommendation.reason: It is the design the repository has already reviewed for T-F3-18 (SOL-P3c-E §3.2) and it respects the settled placement of LLM egress in ms-system-setting, so almost nothing has to be invented. Keeping the quota pre-check and the usage ledger in SVC-01's own transaction gives AC-AI-04 the strict reading the CR asks for ("the system does not call the provider"), which opt-2's edge counters can only approximate, and it delivers the per-org and per-project configuration plus cost limits in full, which opt-3 deliberately reduces. The extra cost over opt-3 is one migration and a quota module, both additive and switched off by `AI_ENABLED` until accepted.

requirement_coverage.note: All three mount the six routes in ms-system-setting, store the user and assistant turns in `ai_conversation_message` and list them via `/ai/conversation/chat/list/:id`, verified against mock-ext's OpenAI endpoint.
The code path is provider-agnostic (OpenAI-compatible), but the repo marks a real LLM as `⏸ ENV B10`: the AC can only be closed once an approved provider, egress and budget exist (Q-2).

Keys stay `enc:v1:` AES-256-GCM (INT-14) via `internal/secret`; API returns `secret.Show`, audit uses `audit.Redact`, aiclient puts the key only in the Authorization header and never in logs, spans or metric labels (NFR-SE-04). The plaintext key still travels on the internal gRPC `ResolveModel` reply and needs its own redaction test.

opt-1 and opt-3 pre-check the organisation's budget inside the request transaction before `ResolveModel`, so no provider call happens; opt-2 refuses at the edge from Redis counters, which is faster but eventually consistent, so it can overshoot the limit in the worst case.

opt-1/opt-3 use a subtree middleware in system-setting (flag from env, or from `system_parameter` in opt-3); opt-2 answers 503 at the gateway. All three conflict with BRL-64/ADR-12/NFR-CO-02's 404 + `X-Route-Missing: 1` rule and need the exception recorded (A-2).

Identical `shared/pkg/aiclient` behaviour in every option: ≤2 retries on 429/5xx/timeout honouring `Retry-After` (capped), then the real error; proven by unit tests and mock-ext `__fail`, which sets `Retry-After`.

The aiclient HTTP client is built from `netguard.FromEnv(netguard.AdminTarget)` per ADR-15/NFR-SE-05, so loopback, link-local, metadata and platform CIDRs are refused with netguard's fixed "target not allowed"; the local stack opens private targets only for mock-ext.

assumptions.text: Pilot assumption carried over from the reviewer's answer: ADR-09 names only Jira and Google, so LLM egress may live in ms-system-setting behind the netguard AdminTarget profile.

AC-5's 503 is read as "a service that is configured off", not as a deferred feature, so it is an explicit documented exception to ADR-12 / BRL-64 / NFR-CO-02 rather than a violation; FR-SYS-07 is revised in the same change.

"Hạn mức" is enforced per organisation and per calendar month, counted on provider-reported prompt/completion tokens with an optional cost ceiling in micro-units; the cap is set by a system administrator.
The SPA is frozen (NFR-CO-01), so the request/response shapes of `/ai/conversation/*` are those of `ui/tms/src/api/modules/ai.ts` and the chat answer is a bare string in the envelope.
AC-1 is proven against tests/local-stack mock-ext `POST /llm/v1/chat/completions` with `MOCK_EXT_STRICT_KEYS=1`, and AC-6 with its `__script {rate_limit, retry_after}` scenario.
Reopening `/ai/conversation/*` at the gateway is in scope for this CR (it is the only way the SPA reaches the routes), including the four governance files that record the current `gone` decision.

conflicts: AC-5 (503 when AI_ENABLED is off) conflicts with BRL-64, NFR-CO-02 and ADR-12, which require a feature without a real implementation to be fully hidden (404 + `X-Route-Missing: 1`) and explicitly reject 501 or fake-200 routes; ADR-12 notes the existing AI 501 exception (OI-02) that this CR removes.

FR-SYS-07, as stated in URD and SRS revision 1, requires chat and transform to answer an honest 501 while AI is not connected, so every option contradicts the current requirement text and needs it revised to revision 2 together with the golden-route and conformance artefacts (NFR-CO-01, NFR-MA-04).
gaps: Nothing in the graph defines an AI quota or cost limit: no entity, attribute, rule or quality target for tokens, money, period or who sets the cap, and docs/features/08-ai-advanced mentions none either.

ENT-17 records conversations as deferred ("hội thoại (hoãn)") with only ai_model_source attributes, so there is no element for ai_conversation_message, for per-organisation/per-project model config (no organization_id/project_id attribute), for the AI_ENABLED flag, for the supported provider list, or for streaming.

open_questions.text: Quota semantics are absent from the knowledge graph and from docs/features/08-ai-advanced: is the limit counted in tokens, in money, or both; per month or rolling; shared by all projects of an organisation; and does an exhausted cap block only chat or every AI feature (CR-H02 generation too)?
Which status code does an exhausted quota return (429 with Retry-After, as NFR-PE-07 does for rate limits, or 402/422), given the SPA only shows the message?

Who signs the amendment that lets a configured-off AI answer 503 instead of the 404 + `X-Route-Missing: 1` that ADR-12 / BRL-64 / NFR-CO-02 require, and does FR-SYS-07 revision 2 ship in this CR or in a documentation change?
Does CR-H02 need token streaming to the browser and provider-specific parameters? If yes, opt-1 must add a server-streaming `AIService.Chat` and opt-2's direct egress becomes cheaper.
Which real provider is approved for AC-2, who supplies the credential, and in which environment is that test run (the repo marks the real-LLM check as environment-blocked)?

Per-project model configuration is not in ENT-17 (no project_id/organization_id attribute): is the resolution order project → organisation → system, and may a project override an organisation's provider while still being charged to that organisation's cap?
Does `AI_ENABLED` also gate the already-live `/ai/config/*` and `/personal/model/*` configuration routes, or only `/ai/conversation/*` as AC-5 states?

options.approach:
Same `aiclient` package, same migrations, same routes and the same gateway flip as opt-1, but a different **trust boundary**.

1. **gRPC contract exactly as approved** — `tms/identity/v1/ai.proto`: `ResolveModel{model_id,user_id,org_id} → {provider_name, base_url, model, api_key(PLAIN), params}`, `ListMessages`, `AppendTurn`, guarded by the existing `grpcx` ACL (`RequireCaller("case-management","api-test")`, `backend/shared/pkg/grpcx/acl.go`). Each caller constructs `aiclient.New(Provider{...})` itself and performs the egress with its own `netguard.FromEnv(netguard.AdminTarget)` client.
2. **Budget as its own contract** — `CheckBudget{org_id, estimated_tokens}` before the call and `RecordUsage{org_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_micro}` after it, writing the INSERT-only `ai_usage_ledger` in ms-system-setting; `/ai/conversation/chat` in SS uses the same pair so there is one code path for the rule, two for the transport.
3. **Key hygiene becomes a test obligation, not a structural property** — client/server gRPC interceptors must redact `api_key` from logs, spans and metric labels (NFR-SE-04); add a dedicated test that greps the span/log sink for the mock key (`tests/local-stack/mock-ext` exposes it at `GET /__keys`), plus a never-return assertion on every HTTP DTO (`secret.Show` already masks `app_key`).
4. **Routes, data, flag, gateway, tests** — identical to opt-1: `ai_conversation` v2 + `ai_conversation_message`, per-project `ai_model_source`, `AI_ENABLED` (off ⇒ 503), `default_table.go:161` gone → system-setting subtree with ≥90 s read timeout, mock-ext `__script {rate_limit}` for AC-6 and `netguard.AllowLoopbackForTests` for AC-7.
5. **Why one would pick this** — CR-H02 (case generation with `JSONMode`, marker parsing, transform retry) and CR-H03 (api-test) call the provider with service-specific prompts, parameters and streaming; having them own the HTTP call avoids a second hop and a server-streaming proxy, and keeps ms-system-setting out of the latency path of long generations.
cons: The decrypted API key crosses an internal gRPC boundary and is held in two more process memories; AC-3 then depends on interceptor redaction and discipline rather than structure, and NFR-SE-04 ("secrets never in log, span, metric label") becomes a per-service obligation.
Spreads egress over three services, so the `netguard` AdminTarget profile and the SSRF/retry policy of NFR-SE-05 must be configured and tested three times; a future consumer can skip the guard.
Check-then-use quota is racy: concurrent chats can each pass `CheckBudget` and overshoot the cap, so AC-4 is only approximately enforced under load.

Centralising credentials and egress is the stated rationale of ADR-09 (named for Jira/Google); handing LLM keys to case-management/api-test moves in the opposite direction even though the decision does not formally cover LLMs.
Carries the same AC-5 conflict with BRL-64 / NFR-CO-02 / ADR-12 and the same FR-SYS-07 revision need as opt-1, plus the same undefined quota semantics (not in the knowledge graph).
pros: Matches a solution document that is already marked ready in the repo, including the SPA call-order race, envelope shapes and the gateway requirements — the least design left to invent and no amendment to that document.
No extra hop and no streaming proxy for CR-H02/H03: each service shapes its own prompt, parameters and SSE handling directly against the provider.
ms-system-setting stays a config/metadata service and does not hold long-lived outbound calls for other services' features.
`CheckBudget`/`RecordUsage` is explicit, so a consumer that forgets it is visible in review and can be caught by a conformance check.

options.approach:
1. **`backend/shared/pkg/aiclient`** — identical to opt-1 (OpenAI-compatible, `netguard` AdminTarget, 60 s, ≤2 retries honouring `Retry-After`, masked key, `ai_requests_total`/`ai_latency_seconds`), because AC-6 and AC-7 are package-level behaviour in every option.
2. **No new gRPC surface** — `ResolveModel/ListMessages/AppendTurn` stay unexported Go functions in `internal/usecase/ai`; nothing outside ms-system-setting can resolve a model, so the key cannot leak by contract (AC-3) and no proto has to be frozen before CR-H02 clarifies what it needs.
3. **Data** — the migration the CR names and nothing more: `ai_conversation` gains `title/scene/organization_id/model_id/update_time`, `ai_conversation_message` is created, `ai_model_source` gains `project_id` (project → org → system resolution). No ledger table, no budget table.
4. **Budget** — limits live in the existing system/organisation settings (`/setting`-family params already served by SS), usage in Redis: `INCRBY ai:usage:<org>:<YYYYMM>` for tokens and cost-micro, checked **before** resolving the model, so an exhausted org gets a 429 with a clear message and no provider call (AC-4). Metrics expose current usage per org for operators.
5. **Routes & flag** — the six `/ai/conversation/*` handlers exactly as the SPA calls them (idempotent on the client `conversationId`, bare string from `chat`, never-nil lists), `AI_ENABLED` off ⇒ 503.
6. **Gateway & governance** — the same unavoidable flip of `default_table.go:161` from `gone` to the system-setting subtree with a ≥90 s read timeout, plus `route_decisions.approved.yaml`, `routes_golden_test.go`, `route_classes_dec.yaml`, `ui_route_decisions.yaml` and a `deferred_features.yaml` row for Claude/Bedrock.
7. **Tests** — aiclient unit tests (Retry-After, blocked private target), handler tests against mock-ext `/llm/v1/chat/completions`, a quota test that asserts mock-ext recorded **no** request after the cap, SEC-07 extension for the AI key.
8. **Follow-up (explicitly out of this slice)** — CR-H02 chooses between an internal signed HTTP route (`/internal/ai/chat`) and the full `AIService` proto once its prompt/streaming needs are known.
cons: A Redis counter is not an INSERT-only journal; BRL-64's enforcement mechanism for this requirement family names exactly that (`nhật ký INSERT-only`), and an operator cannot audit or bill AI usage afterwards.
Losing or flushing Redis silently resets an org's consumption, so the cap in AC-4 is best-effort rather than durable.
CR-H02/H03 will either duplicate model resolution and egress or trigger a second refactor of this layer; the repo's approved SOL-P3c-E §3.2 expects the gRPC contract now.
Carries the same unavoidable conflicts as the other options: AC-5's 503 against BRL-64 / NFR-CO-02 / ADR-12, and the FR-SYS-07 (501) revision.
Per-organisation cost limits stored in generic settings params have no schema validation and no history of who changed a cap.
pros: Smallest blast radius and the fastest path to a working AI chat: no proto, no new owned tables beyond the two the CR names, no cross-service trust decision.
Keeps the plaintext key inside one process for free, so AC-3 needs no interceptor work.
Postpones the one design decision nobody can settle today (what CR-H02 needs from the AI layer) instead of freezing a contract that will be rewritten.
Cheapest to roll back: the flag, four governance rows and two additive tables.
